note: THE RENDERING, which is the other thing packages read out of these plists. Emacs answers ("My error: 1, 2" "My error" "My error: \"boom\"" "peculiar error: 9"): the message, then a comma-separated `prin1' of the data; no data means no colon; a STRING datum is still printed with its quotes; and a symbol with no `error-message' renders as "peculiar error: ...". kg HAS `error-message-string' already, so this case measures the rendering it will have to produce once the plists exist; at this pin it stops at `define-error' being `void-function'.
